evals.name: port-android-screen-to-ios
evals.prompt: I've got a React Native screen that was designed by our Android dev and it looks off on iPhone. It's a settings-ish list: a ScrollView wrapped in <SafeAreaView style={{flex:1, backgroundColor:'#fff'}}>, rows are <TouchableOpacity style={{height: 56, paddingHorizontal: 16}}> with a Text at fontSize 16 color '#333' and a right-side chevron from react-native-vector-icons (MaterialIcons 'chevron-right', size 20). Header is a custom <View style={{height:56, backgroundColor:'#fff', borderBottomWidth:1, borderBottomColor:'#eee'}}> with a centered title. Can you fix it so it feels native on iOS? We're on RN 0.76 with react-navigation 7.
evals.expected_output: Identifies the SafeAreaView-as-outermost-element problem, replaces hex with PlatformColor semantic tokens (grouped background set for a settings list), swaps fixed row height for minHeight, replaces the custom header with a native-stack header (large title / headerTransparent + blur), swaps MaterialIcons chevron for SF Symbols chevron.right, sets 44pt hit targets, fixes lineHeight, and mentions Dynamic Type. Should cite specific HIG numbers.

evals.name: sheet-with-unsaved-changes
evals.prompt: Adding an 'Edit Profile' modal to our RN app (iOS + iPad). It needs a Done button that saves. What's the right way to present it and what do I need to handle?
evals.expected_output: Recommends native-stack formSheet/modal presentation with detents and a visible grabber; insists Done is paired with Cancel; covers intercepting swipe-to-dismiss via beforeRemove and confirming with an ACTION SHEET (not an alert) offering a save option; notes one-sheet-at-a-time and no nested navigator; notes iPad page/form sheet style; mentions title naming the task.

evals.name: tvos-focus-port
evals.prompt: We want to ship our RN iOS app on Apple TV. It's a media browsing app — horizontal rows of 300x170 poster cards, a bottom tab bar, and 17pt captions under each card. What has to change?
evals.expected_output: Explains react-native-tvos as a separate app/fork (no Expo); explains the focus engine (every element focusable, focus via scale+animation not color, five focus states, assets at focused size); computes spacing for focus growth; applies the 60/80pt overscan safe area manually; replaces the iOS type scale with the tvOS one (29pt body Medium, 23pt min) so 17pt captions are called out as unreadable; notes 66pt targets; notes tab bar scroll/pin behavior and Menu=parent-not-previous; mentions Top Shelf needs a Swift extension.

evals.name: liquid-glass-tab-bar
evals.prompt: How do I get that iOS 26 frosted glass look on my bottom tab bar in React Native? Right now I've got tabBarStyle: { backgroundColor: 'rgba(255,255,255,0.8)' } and it looks flat.
evals.expected_output: Explains Liquid Glass is not just blur (luminosity adaptation, specular highlights, content-driven light/dark flip are unreachable from JS); the correct answer is a native tab bar (react-native-bottom-tabs) rather than styling the JS one; says to REMOVE backgroundColor because it overrides the material; covers content scrolling under the bar + safe area padding; covers Reduce Transparency falling back to OPAQUE not weaker blur; covers Android using elevation instead of fake blur; mentions performance constraints.

evals.name: permission-and-accessibility-review
evals.expected_output: Flags: permission requested on mount rather than at point of use, and no denied-path handling / canAskAgain; missing NSCameraUsageDescription purpose string guidance; 10pt text below the 11pt iOS minimum and poor contrast; 28pt hit targets below 44pt (needs hitSlop); no accessibilityRole/accessibilityLabel on either button; icon inside button not hidden from a11y tree; state conveyed by color alone (green/red) with no shape or label; red/green being the classic colorblind failure pair; no accessibilityState. Should cite specific numbers.

evals.name: navigator-structure-iphone-ipad
evals.prompt: Inherited an RN app and the navigation feels off. It uses @react-navigation/stack with a createBottomTabNavigator, four tabs. The header is styled with headerStyle: { backgroundColor: '#fff' } and the tab bar with tabBarStyle: { backgroundColor: '#fff', borderTopWidth: 1 }. There's a search TextInput at the top of the list screen's content. One of the tabs opens a 'New Post' composer. We ship the same build to iPhone and iPad. What should change?
evals.expected_output: Switches @react-navigation/stack to @react-navigation/native-stack as the highest-impact change, naming what it recovers (real push transition, interactive back-swipe, large titles, real sheets). Replaces the JS bottom tabs with react-native-bottom-tabs for a real UITabBarController (material, scroll-under, selection haptic), and notes it is iOS/Android only. Says to REMOVE both backgroundColor values and borderTopWidth because they override the Liquid Glass material; uses headerTransparent + headerBlurEffect + headerShadowVisible: false instead. Moves the search TextInput into headerSearchBarOptions with a scope-conveying placeholder. Flags that the 'New Post' tab violates the rule that every tab is a destination — it should be a toolbar button presenting a sheet, not a tab. For iPad, adapts the tab bar to a sidebar via tabBarPosition: 'left' driven by useWindowDimensions(), not Platform.isPad. Mentions headerLargeTitle needing contentInsetAdjustmentBehavior='automatic'.

evals.name: list-dynamic-type-vs-perf
evals.prompt: Accessibility audit came back on our RN feed: at the larger text sizes the row labels get cut off. The rows are <View style={{height: 56, paddingHorizontal: 16}}> inside a FlatList that has getItemLayout={(d, i) => ({length: 56, offset: 56 * i, index: i})}. Each row is a 44x44 thumbnail, a title, a subtitle, and a chevron. I need to fix the truncation but this list can be 5000 items and it has to stay smooth. How do I do both?
evals.expected_output: Names the actual conflict: the HIG requires minHeight (Dynamic Type) while getItemLayout requires a known fixed height, so they are incompatible and fixing the height is the wrong resolution. Prescribes minHeight (>= 44) plus vertical padding instead of height: 56. Says getItemLayout must be REMOVED rather than recomputed, and that correct layout at AX5 outranks scroll-position precision. Recommends FlashList v2 as the resolution because it measures rendered items and needs no size estimates — and notes v2 removed estimatedItemSize / estimatedListSize / estimatedFirstItemOffset, so those props should not be added. Adds flexShrink: 1 on the label so it wraps instead of pushing the chevron off the row. Mentions recyclingKey on the thumbnail to stop the wrong image flashing into a recycled row. Treats the row as a single accessibility focus stop with a composed label, with the thumbnail and chevron hidden from the a11y tree. Says to verify at the largest accessibility text size. Should NOT recommend hard-coding a larger fixed height or disabling allowFontScaling.
